tagline.text: A small island where you meet thresher sharks in the dawn sea

children.text: A small island roughly
2.5km

long, floating in the sea off the northernmost tip of Cebu Island — one of the few dive spots in the world where thresher sharks can be seen almost daily. Car-free lanes and white sand beaches make it a favorite of divers and holidaymakers alike.
Malapascua is a small island about
30–45 minutes
by bangka from Maya Port at the northern tip of mainland Cebu. It measures roughly
2.5km
from north to south and just over
1km

across — small enough to walk around in a loop. There are almost no cars on the island; motorcycle taxis and pedestrians share the sandy, dirt lanes instead. Administratively it belongs to the municipality of Daanbantayan, Cebu.
There is one reason this island is famous worldwide: the thresher shark. At Monad Shoal, an underwater plateau about
8km

off the island's east coast, deep-dwelling thresher sharks rise every dawn to let cleaner wrasse pick parasites off their bodies — a spot where they can be observed almost daily, a rarity anywhere in the world. Divers rank the sight of one gliding past with its long, scythe-shaped tail fin among the scenes you must see at least once in a lifetime.
Most of the island was badly damaged by Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan) in

, but the resorts and dive shops that were rebuilt afterward actually left it looking tidier than before. With more than twenty dive centers clustered here, many beginners come to take their Open Water certification course, and even travelers who don't dive find plenty of reasons to visit — Bounty Beach's fine white sand, a day trip to Kalanggaman Island, and the quiet fishing-village scenery.

It's quieter and more reasonably priced than resort-heavy destinations like Boracay or Panglao, which makes it especially well suited to travelers whose main goal is diving, or to couples wanting an uncrowded island getaway. Since it takes
5–6 hours
from Cebu City by land and sea combined, at least two nights are recommended.

blocks.title: Thresher shark diving at Monad Shoal

children.text: Boats leave between
to wait for thresher sharks at a cleaning station around

deep. Chances are highest just before and after sunrise. An Open Water certification is enough to join, but given the depth, having an Advanced certification or deep-diving experience makes it much more comfortable.
About
1 hour

by boat from Malapascua, Gato Island is a marine protected area where you can see whitetip reef sharks resting under rocks, sea snakes, cuttlefish, and seahorses. A short underwater cave tunnel running through one side of the island is a standout feature.
A sandbar island belonging to Palompon, Leyte, about
1.5–2 hours
from Malapascua by bangka, famous in drone photos for the long sandbars stretching from each end. Boat charter and entrance fees combined get cheaper the more people join.

blocks.title: Watching the sunset at Bounty Beach

children.text: Bounty Beach on the island's south side is a nearly
1km
stretch of white sand lined with resorts and restaurants. The shallow water in the afternoon is good for swimming, and the row of bangkas at dusk makes for a beautiful scene.

blocks.title: Walking a loop of the island

children.text: In about
2–3 hours

on foot, you can take in the lighthouse on the north end, Logon village to the west, and the quiet east coast. Along the way you'll see village children, a cockfighting arena, and a small chapel — glimpses of simple island life up close.

If you don't dive, a half-day boat tour lets you snorkel over the coral areas and shallow coral gardens around the island. Small marine life is abundant, making it a good spot for anyone who enjoys macro photography.
At dusk, a sunset dive at nearby Lighthouse Point to watch the brightly patterned mandarinfish mate is popular. It's over quickly, so it's easy to fit into even a tight schedule.

It takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
from Manila to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), with dozens of daily flights from Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific, and others. One-way fares run about
. From Korea, there are daily direct flights to Cebu from Incheon and Busan.
Take a Ceres bus to Maya from the North Bus Terminal next to SM City Cebu. Buses run about every
30 minutes to 1 hour
, the trip takes
4–5 hours
, and the fare is about
. From Mactan Airport to the terminal, a Grab or taxi takes
40 minutes to 1 hour
(about
). To save time, you can also charter a private van or Grab straight from the airport to Maya Port (about
3–4 hours
Shared bangkas to Malapascua leave Maya Port once they fill with passengers, at about
and taking
30–45 minutes
. Scheduled bangkas stop running around
, so if you arrive late you will have to charter a boat (about

), and you pay the environmental fee at the port tourism counter. At low tide or on days with high waves, the bangka often cannot pull up close to the beach, so you frequently wade knee- to thigh-deep water to board and disembark.
Roads on the island are narrow, so motorcycle taxis (habal-habal) and walking are your only options. It's about
from the port to accommodations on Bounty Beach.
The dry season,
December–May
, is good overall, but during
December–February
the northeast monsoon (Amihan) roughens the sea east of the island, making bangkas rock and the trip to Monad Shoal choppy. The sea is calmest and underwater visibility best from
March to June
, when water temperatures also rise to 27–29°C, making diving more comfortable.
June–November
is the rainy season and the southwest monsoon (Habagat) period, with frequent afternoon showers, and from
August to November

typhoons sometimes pass through northern Visayas, occasionally halting sea travel entirely. Thresher sharks are seen year-round, but the odds vary with weather and current, so scheduling dawn dives on two or more mornings reduces the chance of missing them.
Around the third week of
January
, during Cebu City's Sinulog Festival, traffic in Cebu gets very congested, so allow extra travel time.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
Most accommodations are clustered along Bounty Beach on the island's south side. Beachfront resorts run about
a night, and many also run their own dive shop, which is convenient for dawn dives. To save money, guesthouses in the village behind Bounty Beach offer air-conditioned rooms for around
. Logon village on the island's west side is quieter with good sunsets, but has fewer restaurant options.

Given how many divers visit, there are plenty of Western-style cafes and pizza and pasta places, while local eateries serve grilled fish and squid, adobo, and sinigang — Filipino home-style dishes — for about

. In the evenings, Bounty Beach restaurants set up tables right on the sand and cook that day's catch priced by weight. Dive shops often only provide coffee and bread before dawn dives, so it's a good idea to bring your own snack.
ATMs on the island are few and often out of order or out of cash, so withdraw enough in Cebu City or in Bogo/Daanbantayan on the way to Maya. Dive shop card payments often carry a 3–5% surcharge.
Thresher shark dives are popular, so during peak season (
March–May
, Holy Week) you need to book at least a day ahead. Asking about a diving package when you book your accommodation can get you a discount.
You'll often get wet boarding or disembarking bangkas, so bring a waterproof bag and sandals; a backpack is much more practical than a rolling suitcase.
Dawn dives go down close to
before sunrise, so bringing a 5mm wetsuit or a hooded vest will help you stay warmer.
Strobe lights are banned at Monad Shoal. Set your camera for natural light.
Phone signal reaches most of the island but is slow. Accommodation Wi-Fi also goes down during power outages, so it's best to handle anything important before you leave Cebu.
Good photo spots are the Bounty Beach sunset, the north lighthouse, and the Kalanggaman Island sandbar. Drones are allowed on Kalanggaman, but check the on-site rules first.

There is no proper clinic on the island, so even minor treatment means going to the main island, and the decompression chamber is in Cebu City. Take out diver insurance and bring a generous supply of basic medicines.
You must wait at least
18–24 hours
after diving before flying. Be sure to schedule your last dive with your departure flight from Cebu Airport in mind.
Thresher sharks won't attack people, but they're timid and flee easily. Stay behind the rope at the cleaning station and don't chase them or reach out.
Sea travel can be suspended during
January–February
and when typhoons approach. Avoid staying on the island right up until your departure and leave at least a day of buffer.
Stepping on coral or taking shells from the beach and sea is prohibited and can result in a fine.
The island's lanes have few streetlights and get very dark at night. Bring a flashlight, and don't walk alone on remote beaches after dark.
Don't drink tap water — use bottled water instead. Most ice is made from purified water, but it's safer to be cautious at small street stalls.
On
September 30, 2025
, a magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck off Daanbantayan, causing heavy damage in northern Cebu, including the collapse of the Daanbantayan church, and in
November 2025

Typhoon Tino (Kalmaegi) followed. Malapascua's resorts and dive shops have been receiving guests again since late that year, but aftershocks and reconstruction work may continue, so check your accommodation's evacuation instructions and read the latest local news before you leave.
